headline: Working paper finds AI-native startups have lower entry-level shares and flatter structures
summary: Harvard Business School Working Paper 26-090 analyzes U.S. venture-backed startup workforce data linked to Y Combinator cohorts and PitchBook records. The authors report entry-level employee shares 4 percentage points lower in the Y Combinator sample (2,233 firms) and 6 points lower in the broader PitchBook sample (41,214 firms). Adjusted firm-size estimates are about 25% smaller for Y Combinator AI-tagged firms and 12% smaller for PitchBook; estimated hierarchy differences are about 0.5 fewer levels and 0.146 fewer levels, respectively. AI status comes from founders’ public tags for Y Combinator and a text classifier for PitchBook; the workforce records end in January 2025. This cross-sectional draft does not identify whether AI caused the organizational differences or imply aggregate job losses: founder selection, product design, startup entry and other firm differences remain possible explanations.
